newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: A$ in comfort zone, benefits miners -govt minister.
newsitem.headline: A$ in comfort zone, benefits miners -govt minister.

text.p: Australia's mining industry was benefitting from the recent fall in the value of the Australian dollar, which now appeared to be in comfort zone, Resources and Energy Minister Warwick Parer said on Monday.
"Most people in the mining industry are pretty comfortable with the dollar as it stands now," Parer told reporters after addressing a mining conference on Monday.
Last December the dollar reached a six year high above US$0.82, but has since fallen, weighed down by interest rate cuts and speculation more reductions are likely.
Earlier this month it reached an 18-month low of US$0.7310, and at 1.30 p.m. (0330 GMT) on Monday it was trading at US$0.7375/80.
Parer declined to forecast any future movements in the Australian dollar, but said the currency was currently in "a comfort zone".
A lower valued Australian dollar makes Australian exports more competitive.
Parer declined to forecast any changes in Australian interest rates after earlier telling the conference that he would like to see them come down further.
